subject: civil
audience: FE Civil candidates and civil engineering students
title: The Beam Reactions That Refused to Split 50-50
featured_title: THE BEAM REACTIONS THAT REFUSED TO SPLIT 50-50

presentation.challenge: The total load was 28 kN, but the support reactions were not 14 kN each.

practice.primary_question: Why do simply supported beam reactions depend on load position, not just total load?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Splitting the total vertical load equally between supports without taking moments about a support.

case_dna.target_misconception: A simply supported beam always divides its vertical load equally between the two supports.
case_dna.why_plausible: Equal reactions occur for symmetric loading, so that special case is easy to overgeneralize.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For a 6 m span with 8 kN at 1 m and 20 kN at 4 m from support A, moment equilibrium gives RB=(8×1+20×4)/6=14.67 kN and RA=13.33 kN.
case_dna.corrected_model: Use both force equilibrium and moment equilibrium. Load location controls the reaction distribution.

problem_statement: A simply supported 6 m beam has a pin at A and a roller at B. An 8 kN downward load acts 1 m from A, and a 20 kN downward load acts 4 m from A. A quick check assigns 14 kN to each support because the total load is 28 kN. Calculate the actual reactions and identify why the equal split is incorrect.
fixed_constraints: 8 kN load at x=1 m from A
20 kN load at x=4 m from A

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The vertical forces summed correctly. The moments did not.
facts: Load 1: 8 kN at 1 m from A
Load 2: 20 kN at 4 m from A
gates.prompt: What equation determines how the 28 kN is distributed between A and B?

options.label: Use ΣFy=0 and ΣM=0; reaction values depend on load positions
options.reason: Rigid-body equilibrium requires both force and moment balance.

options.label: Set RA=RB=14 kN because there are two supports
options.reason: That satisfies vertical force balance but not necessarily moment balance.

options.label: Assign each load entirely to the nearest support
options.reason: Support reactions follow whole-body equilibrium, not nearest-support assignment.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict reaction at B
gates.prompt: Using moments about A, what is RB in kN?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Read the support reactions
gates.result: Reaction B is about 14.67 kN and reaction A is about 13.33 kN.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the reaction at B
gates.hint: Take moments about A so RA drops out.

cards.text: RB must create 88 kN·m counter-moment: RB(6)=88.
RB≈14.67 kN and RA≈13.33 kN satisfy both ΣFy=0 and ΣMA=0.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the beam-reaction note
report: C1. Total downward load is 28 kN.
C2. There are two vertical support reactions.
C3. Therefore each support reaction is 14 kN.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: The pin and roller provide vertical reactions here.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: Equal force sharing ignores the moments created by the different load locations.

evidence_choices.label: RB(6)=8(1)+20(4), so RB≈14.67 kN
evidence_choices.reason: This is the moment-equilibrium condition about A.

correction.template: The reactions are approximately RA={ra} kN and RB={rb} kN.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Make the reactions equal without changing the 28 kN total load
gates.constraint: Keep a 6 m simply supported span.

options.label: Arrange the resultant 28 kN load to act at midspan, x=3 m
options.reason: A centered resultant gives equal reactions of 14 kN each.

options.label: Move the resultant closer to B
options.reason: That makes RB larger than RA.

options.label: Move the resultant closer to A
options.reason: That makes RA larger than RB.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply beam equilibrium
gates.prompt: A 4 m simply supported beam carries a single 12 kN load at midspan. What is each vertical reaction?

options.label: 6 kN
options.reason: Symmetric loading gives equal reactions summing to 12 kN.

options.label: 12 kN
options.reason: That would produce 24 kN total upward force.

options.label: 3 kN
options.reason: The reactions must sum to the 12 kN load.

gates.explanation: Equal reactions occur here because both the support geometry and the loading are symmetric.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the rigid-body equilibrium
gates.confirmation: I confirm that beam reactions must satisfy both force and moment equilibrium.

items.label: What failed
items.value: The reaction split was based only on total force.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The loads create unequal moments about the supports.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use ΣF=0 and ΣM=0 on the complete beam free-body diagram.

seo.seo_title: Simply Supported Beam Reactions: Why Loads Do Not Split 50-50 | FE E-042
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Civil Case E-042: a 6 m beam with 8 kN and 20 kN point loads has reactions 13.33 and 14.67 kN, not 14 kN each.
seo.excerpt: Support reactions depend on where the loads act. Force balance alone cannot determine the distribution.
seo.direct_answer: For a 6 m simply supported beam with 8 kN at 1 m and 20 kN at 4 m from A, moment equilibrium about A gives RB(6)=8(1)+20(4)=88, so RB≈14.67 kN. Vertical equilibrium then gives RA≈13.33 kN.

faqs.q: Do simply supported beam reactions always split equally?
faqs.a: No. Equal reactions occur only for appropriate symmetric loading.

faqs.q: Why take moments about a support?
faqs.a: It removes that support reaction from the moment equation and lets the other reaction be solved directly.
